hinglish.source: the first six reels posted by hand, read from Instagram insights
keep: A question nearly everyone has asked themselves, with the answer held back: the Aadhaar PDF password reel got 1,900 views, 22 saves, 8 shares and 3 follows in a few hours, more than all other reels together
Opening on a character in a situation (night desk scene) with a curiosity question: skip rate 37-39%, better than typical
Everyday documents every Indian adult handles (Aadhaar, PAN, passport photo, bank statement) travel further than narrow exam-form problems
Useful how-to content people want to keep: save rates above typical
avoid: Opening on an error card or a product-style headline: skip rate jumped to 57%
Reels over about 25 seconds: average watch time is only 8-9 seconds
Flat, rushed narration with no pauses
next_tests: A different tool every post in week 1
Answer revealed in the last third
Ending on a line worth sending to a friend, to lift shares

keep: Hooks that tell the viewer what they get for free or on the site (the two top reels average 8-9s watched, versus 1.7-7s for the others). This is based on only two reels and is not proven.
Keep reels very short or simple. The top two had the longest average watch time (8.1s and 9.4s) even though they have no real hook style.
Use a hashtag or community-style opener (#ilovedocuments). It earned 18 shares from 198 reach, the most shares of any reel.
Point viewers to the website or to multiple tools. The 'check our website' reel had the highest reach (298) and the only like and save combination among the top reels.
Show a concrete problem a viewer might have (4 photos into one PDF). It held attention better (7.0s) than the cheat sheet (4.0s), though it got no engagement.
avoid: Broad promise hooks with emoji and no specific problem ('Any PDF or photo job – one free website 👇'). It had the lowest average watch time (1.7s) and almost no engagement.
Long reels (31-32s) with scripted formats (secret_answer, cheat_sheet). Both had low average watch (4-7s, a small fraction of the length) and zero likes or comments on the question reel.
Bold or negative claims about paying a cyber cafe. It got 146 views, 1 like and 2 saves, and viewers watched only 4s on average.
Anything that gets zero shares and zero comments. Three of the five reels had no shares and no comments, so none of the formats are producing conversation yet.
next_tests: Make the same 'How do you send 4 photos as one PDF?' question reel at about 10-15s instead of 31s, and compare average watch time with the 31s version (7.0s).

Re-post the 'check our website, multiple tools' message with a specific tool named in the first 2 seconds (for example merge PDF). Check whether reach stays near 300 and whether average watch stays above 8s.
Test a hashtag or community opener (like #ilovedocuments) on a specific-problem reel such as jpg_to_pdf. The goal is to see whether the shares (18) come from the opener or from the topic.
